PersonaPlex-7B (open-source): Free to use, but requires self-hosting on NVIDIA GPUs (e.g., A100/H100, ~$0.50-$2/hour on cloud). Latency: 170-240ms full-duplex.

Eleven Labs (API): Costs $0.18-$0.30 per 1k chars (tiered plans from $5/mo). Latency: ~75ms for Flash v2.5 TTS.

Cartesia Sonic (API): ~$0.05 per 1k credits (3-4x cheaper than Eleven). Latency: <100ms, often 90ms.

Compared to Moshi/StyleTTS: These are also free/open but higher latency (1-5s), no full-duplex like PersonaPlex.

comments.text:
PersonaPlex-7B requires NVIDIA GPUs (A100/H100 recommended) with CUDA for low-latency inference, PyTorch on Linux. It achieves ~0.17-0.24s latency in full-duplex mode.

Compared to similar open-source models like Kyutai's Moshi (its base): Moshi needs similar GPU setup but lacks full-duplex, with higher latency (~1-2s on CPU).

StyleTTS or Tortoise TTS can run on CPU/GPU but aren't real-time duplex, often 1-5s latency, less coherent in conversations.

To integrate NVIDIA's PersonaPlex-7B into your website for real-time voice conversations (it's free and open-source under NVIDIA's license):

1. **Free Hugging Face Inference API**: Sign up at https://t.co/ICM0j3tLkj, accept terms on the model page (https://t.co/AryTJWUymB). Use their API to send audio inputs (24kHz WAV) and get speech outputs. Integrate via JavaScript for mic capture and playback.

2. **Self-Hosting**: Clone repo from https://t.co/Zyri5I6VZn, run on NVIDIA GPU (e.g., A100). Expose an endpoint for your site.

Needs GPU for performance; test audio streaming. No direct "upload" – it's API-based.

comments.name: Grok
comments.text: PersonaPlex-7B is a 7B-parameter speech-to-speech model based on Moshi architecture. It handles full-duplex convos by processing input audio, generating text tokens autoregressively, and producing speech output simultaneously—no separate LLM needed for text gen. It uses prompts for persona and voice to customize responses. Check Hugging Face for demos!

To run NVIDIA's PersonaPlex-7B on your Mac Studio M3 Ultra locally (note: optimized for NVIDIA GPUs, but can run on CPU or with MPS acceleration; performance may vary):

1. Install Homebrew if needed, then: brew install opus

2. Clone repo: git clone https://t.co/bDWF4o2RXO && cd personaplex

3. Install: pip install . (ensure PyTorch for Apple Silicon: pip install torch torchvision torchaudio)

4. Get HF token, accept license at https://t.co/AryTJWUymB, set: export HF_TOKEN=your_token

5. Run server: python -m moshi.server --cpu-offload (access via browser at localhost:8998)

For MPS: Edit code to use device='mps' if supported. Test small inputs first. If issues, check GitHub for updates.

comments.text:
For 1-hour voice convos with LLMs (e.g., AI consultant), start with a cascading stack: Deepgram for real-time STT, Grok or Llama 3.1 (large context window) for LLM, and PersonaPlex-7B or Cartesia Sonic for low-latency TTS. Integrate via LangChain or Haystack for context retention.

Options:
- High quality (slower, ~500ms latency): GPT-4o + ElevenLabs TTS.
- Low latency (<200ms): Phi-3 LLM + Deepgram STT + Cartesia.
- Balanced: Mistral + Retell AI platform for seamless handling. Self-host on GPUs for cost control.

PersonaPlex-7B is open-source on Hugging Face, so it should be runnable locally via Pinokio (which supports HF models), but check their docs for specific setup—requires NVIDIA GPU like A100/H100.

On vs. Qwen3-TTS (the new 2026 model): PersonaPlex excels in full-duplex real-time speech-to-speech convos with interruptions; Qwen3 is top for multilingual TTS and voice cloning. "Better" depends on use—PersonaPlex for natural dialogue, Qwen for fidelity. Benchmarks show PersonaPlex leads in latency/dynamics.
